headlines.title: Why Retail Investors Are Watching PepsiCo Stock And Other Defensive Dividend Names
headlines.summary: A hotter jobs market and the prospect of higher-for-longer interest rates are quietly reshuffling which stocks feel pressure and which quietly collect the benefits. Income-focused investors risk missing an underappreciated pocket of opportunity if they only watch growth stories. This article walks through three large-cap, rate-sensitive value and dividend stocks that are directly exposed to the latest labor and Fed narrative, and explains why each one deserves a closer look right now.

headlines.title: Kraft Heinz vs. PepsiCo: Consumer Staples Stocks Don't Guarantee Steady Revenue Growth
headlines.summary: PepsiCo's quarterly revenue swings between $17.9 billion and $29.3 billion, while Kraft Heinz hovers consistently near $6 billion—a gap that reveals starkly different business models.

headlines.title: Pepsi’s Stock Has Fallen About a Third From Its Peak. A Gen X Investor Who Grew Up With the Brand Could Be Taking More Risk Than She Realizes
headlines.summary: PepsiCo has lost nearly a third of its value since 2023, and a brand you grew up loving can quietly disguise just how much retirement risk is sitting in your 401(k) right now.

headlines.title: PepsiCo (PEP) vs. KO and MDLZ: Is Its Beverage-and-Snacks Strategy Creating a Stronger Defensive Business?
headlines.summary: Is PEP a good stock to buy? We came across a bullish thesis on PepsiCo, Inc. on Investing Lawyer’s Substack. Since the thesis was published on June 26th, PEP shares have pulled back as investors remain cautious about the pace of its recovery, creating a near-term headwind while its dividend continues to support the income-focused bullish case.

headlines.title: Why Is PepsiCo Stock Falling, and Is It a Buying Opportunity?
headlines.summary: PepsiCo is facing some headwinds, but a consistent dividend and growing international business present an interesting opportunity for investors.

description: PepsiCo, Inc. engages in the manufacture, marketing, distribution, and sale of various beverages and convenient foods worldwide. The company operates through six segments: PepsiCo Foods North America; PepsiCo Beverages North America; International Beverages Franchise; Europe, Middle East and Africa; Latin America Foods; and Asia Pacific Foods. It offers cereals, chips, dips, granola bars, oatmeal, pasta, rice, and syrups and mixes; refrigerated dips and spreads; beverage concentrates, fountain syrups, and finished goods; and ready-to-drink tea and coffee products. The company also provides SodaStream sparkling water makers and related products, as well as various dairy products under the Agusha, Chudo, and Domik v Derevne brands. It serves wholesale and other distributors, foodservice customers, grocery stores, drug stores, convenience stores, discount/dollar stores, mass merchandisers, membership stores, hard discounters, e-commerce retailers and authorized independent bottlers, and others through a network of direct-store-delivery, customer warehouse, and distributor networks, as well as directly to consumers through e-commerce platforms and retailers. PepsiCo, Inc. was founded in 1898 and is based in Purchase, New York.
